newsitem.title: USA: Study says Alaska natural gas project feasible.
newsitem.headline: Study says Alaska natural gas project feasible.

text.p: A huge pipeline project to deliver Alaska North Slope natural gas to Asian markets could be viable if construction costs are reduced from the current $15 billion estimate and developers get some tax breaks, according to a study released by state officials on Friday.
The study gives project promoters cause for optimism, said Gov. Tony Knowles.
Most estimates put the probable gasline startup date at about 2005.

"Alaska's estimated 35 trillion cubic feet of North Slope gas is marketable," Knowles said in a news conference, where he released the study. "The long-discussed Alaska natural gas pipeline project is feasible."

For decades, Alaska governors and other state officials have sought to develop the North Slope's gas reserves to supplant dwindling oil production. However, the need to build a new pipeline -- most likely to parallel the current trans-Alaska oil line -- has made the cost of delivering the gas prohibitive.

Among 13 natural gas projects being planned around the world, the Alaska project would be the biggest, providing 14.5 metric tons of gas a year, according to the study. That far exceeds the scope of the Natuna I project in Indonesia, forecast to provide 7 metric tons a year.

Major owners of Alaska's North Slope gas are Exxon, Atlantic Richfield and British Petroleum, the main leaseholders on North Slope oil fields. The state has a royalty interest in the gas, generally 12.5 percent.
Knowles said he is considering legislation to provide state tax incentives to make the project more competitive.
The project would also get a boost from federal tax changes, including new depreciation schedules and advance tax credits, he said.
Knowles said an Alaska gas project would produce great benefits to the nation.

"The federal governement has the chance to make a significant change in out balance-of-trade deficit with this project," he said. "It's been estimated, up to 10 percent of our balance of trade deficit deficit, right off the top, is cured by this."

In addition to $20 billion to $30 billion in federal receipts, coming in at a rate of $1 billion a year, the project would "generate jobs in the economy as we go about gearing up to build the largest single private project ever built in America."
